---
title: Path to a usable v1
---

The development branch now includes a practical synthetic starter, a shared
staged renderer, preserved script-backend compatibility, and guarded config/skill
upgrades. It remains a review candidate, without a release or public deployment.

## Implemented

- `init` creates a new fictional workspace without overwriting existing files.
- `build` and `build --watch` use builtin or reviewed script renderers.
- Upgrade plans show diffs; application checks hashes, keeps backups and preserves
  customized instructions. QMD, evidence and owner instructions are protected.
- One checksummed wheel is installed in native Windows/macOS rendering CI.
- Synthetic acceptance covers PDF/Word, save watching, failure retention, recovery,
  lock exclusion and interruption of an active TeX process tree.
- Private docs artifacts contain embedded HTML and a single-file guide, so preview
  no longer depends on a localhost server on the reader's own device.

## Verification {#verification}

The expanded local suite has 26 passing tests. Real clean-installed macOS
acceptance passed both backends using only fictional inputs. Native Windows
and macOS rendering results for the final revision belong to the PR's
“Installed starter rendering” workflow; unit CI is reported separately.

Existing private CV wording, evidence and layout remain unchanged. Personal
Calibri output is not inferred from the generic starter's free TeX-font tests.
Word files are checked for content/package validity; Word application pagination
is not certified by PDF checks.

## Remaining before release

1. Verify the final native rendering matrix and review its artifacts, including
   Windows output/source sharing cases where supported.
2. Exercise an owner-led first-use interview/import and tailored selection against
   real evidence, with explicit review of uncertainty. No autonomous collector.
3. Validate source-distribution installation and config/skill migrations across
   future versions, then document the supported version policy.
4. Review all packaging, template/font notices and docs accessibility; choose the
   release version and authorize a release separately.

The architecture does not need a service or database for this workflow.
